source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 2 (PDF 36-50, printed 33-47); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 2 (Bacteria and Viruses), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 The five-kingdom classification system was proposed by:
blocks.explanation: The five-kingdom system was proposed by Robert H. Whittaker (2.1).

book_ref.quote: the five-kingdom classification system, proposed by Robert H. Whittaker

blocks.prompt: 2 In the five-kingdom system, all prokaryotes are placed in the kingdom:
blocks.explanation: All prokaryotes are included in a separate kingdom, Monera; the other four kingdoms are eukaryotes (2.1).

book_ref.quote: all prokaryotes are included in a separate kingdom i.e., the kingdom Monera

blocks.prompt: 3 Because molecular studies highlighted flaws in the five-kingdom system, most biologists favour:
blocks.explanation: Most biologists favour replacing it with the three-domain system, which fits molecular data better (2.1).

book_ref.quote: most biologists favour replacing it with a new system, called three-domain system

blocks.prompt: 4 All bacteria have a unicellular prokaryotic organization that lacks:

options.text: membrane-bounded organelles, including a well-defined nucleus

blocks.explanation: Bacteria lack membrane-bounded organelles including a well-defined nucleus; they have the simplest cellular organization (2.1).

book_ref.quote: which lack membrane bounded organelles, including a well-defined nucleus

blocks.prompt: 5 The major component of the bacterial cell wall is:
blocks.explanation: The major component of the bacterial cell wall is a unique macromolecule, peptidoglycan or murein (2.1).

book_ref.quote: called peptidoglycan or murein

blocks.prompt: 6 The technique of Gram's staining was devised by:
blocks.explanation: Sir Hans Christian Gram devised Gram's staining (2.1).

book_ref.quote: Sir Hans Christian Gram devised the technique of Gram’s staining

blocks.prompt: 7 Gram-positive bacteria stain purple because they:
blocks.explanation: Gram-positive bacteria retain violet dye and stain purple; Gram-negative do not retain it and appear in original colour (2.1).

book_ref.quote: Gram-positive bacteria stain purple because they retain violet dye

blocks.prompt: 8 The cell wall of Gram-positive bacteria has:

options.text: a thin peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane
a thick peptidoglycan layer and less lipid

blocks.explanation: Gram-positive walls have a thick peptidoglycan layer and less lipid; Gram-negative walls have a thin layer and an outer membrane (2.1).

book_ref.quote: The cell wall of Gram-positive bacteria contains thick layer of peptidoglycan and has less lipid content

blocks.prompt: 9 Porin is a protein of the Gram-negative outer membrane that:

options.text: acts like a pore for specific molecules

blocks.explanation: Porin in the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria acts like a pore for specific molecules (2.1).

book_ref.quote: It contains a protein called porin, which acts like a pore for specific molecules

blocks.prompt: 10 Gram-negative bacteria are resistant to many antibiotics because of their:
blocks.explanation: The outer membrane of lipopolysaccharides and lipoproteins makes Gram-negative bacteria resistant to many antibiotics (2.1).

book_ref.quote: The outer membrane makes Gram-negative bacteria resistant to many antibiotics

blocks.prompt: 11 The periplasmic space is the space between:

options.text: the peptidoglycan layer and the cell membrane
the capsule and the cell wall

blocks.explanation: Periplasmic space lies between the peptidoglycan layer and the cell membrane; Gram-negative bacteria have more of it (2.1).

book_ref.quote: space between peptidoglycan layer and cell membrane

blocks.prompt: 12 The capsule produced by some bacteria outside the cell wall is a:
blocks.explanation: The capsule is a gelatinous layer outside the cell wall that gives sticky character to colonies (2.1).

book_ref.quote: It is a gelatinous layer and gives sticky characters to bacterial colonies

blocks.prompt: 13 The bacterial cell membrane differs from that of eukaryotes in that it lacks:
blocks.explanation: The bacterial cell membrane does not have sterols (e.g., cholesterol) in its chemical makeup (2.1).

book_ref.quote: The cell membrane of bacteria does not have sterols

blocks.prompt: 14 In bacteria that lack a cell wall, the outermost layer is the:
blocks.explanation: The cell membrane lies outermost in bacteria that lack a cell wall, i.e., mycoplasmas and spiroplasmas (2.1).

book_ref.quote: It lies at the outermost in bacteria that lack cell wall

blocks.prompt: 15 Mesosomes are formed by:

options.text: folding of the cell wall outwards
invagination of the cell membrane into the cytoplasm

blocks.explanation: At some points the cell membrane invaginates to form vesicles, tubules or lamellae: the mesosomes (2.1).

book_ref.quote: At some points, cell membrane invaginates and forms vesicles, tubules or lamellae in cytoplasm

blocks.prompt: 16 Bacterial cytoplasm lacks:
blocks.explanation: Cytoplasm contains nucleoid, ribosomes and mesosomes but lacks a cytoskeleton and membrane-bounded organelles (2.1).

book_ref.quote: It lacks cytoskeleton and membrane-bounded organelles

blocks.prompt: 17 Bacterial ribosomes sediment at:
blocks.explanation: Each bacterial ribosome sediments at 70S, made of 50S and 30S subunits (2.1).

book_ref.quote: Each ribosome sediments at 70S

blocks.prompt: 18 The smaller subunit of a bacterial ribosome sediments at:
blocks.explanation: The larger subunit is 50S and the smaller subunit is 30S (2.1).

book_ref.quote: larger subunit at 50S and smaller subunit at 30S

blocks.prompt: 19 The irregular-shaped dense area near the centre of the bacterial cytoplasm that contains DNA is the:
blocks.explanation: The nucleoid is an irregular-shaped dense area near the centre that contains DNA (2.1).

book_ref.quote: Near the centre of cytoplasm, there is an irregular-shaped dense area i.e., nucleoid

blocks.prompt: 20 Bacterial DNA differs from eukaryotic chromosomal DNA in that it:

options.text: is enclosed in a nuclear envelope

blocks.explanation: Bacterial DNA is single, circular and double stranded, without attached histones (2.1).

book_ref.quote: Bacterial DNA does not have attached histones

blocks.prompt: 21 Plasmids are:
blocks.explanation: Plasmids are circular, double-stranded extrachromosomal DNA that are self-replicating (2.1).

book_ref.quote: They are self-replicating and can replicate before or after division

blocks.prompt: 22 In genetic engineering, plasmids are used as:

options.text: vectors carrying selected genes into bacteria

blocks.explanation: Plasmids serve as vectors to carry selected genes to bacteria for cloning or synthesis of specific proteins (2.1).

book_ref.quote: They are used to carry selected genes to bacteria for cloning

blocks.prompt: 23 Endospores are:
blocks.explanation: Endospores are specialized resting cells that are thick-walled and metabolically inactive (dormant) (2.2).

book_ref.quote: Endospores are thick-walled and metabolically inactive

blocks.prompt: 24 The first step of sporulation, when a bacterium faces unfavourable conditions, is:
blocks.explanation: Facing unfavourable conditions, the bacterium first replicates its DNA (2.2).

book_ref.quote: When a bacterium faces unfavourable conditions, it replicates its DNA

blocks.prompt: 25 During sporulation, the new DNA and a small portion of cytoplasm are isolated by a:

options.text: septum made by the cell membrane

blocks.explanation: The cell membrane makes a septum to isolate the new DNA and a small portion of cytoplasm (2.2).

book_ref.quote: Cell membrane makes a septum to isolate the new DNA and a small portion of cytoplasm

blocks.prompt: 26 In a developing endospore, the new DNA is surrounded by:
blocks.explanation: The cell membrane grows again around the new DNA, cytoplasm and septum, so the new DNA is surrounded by two membranes (2.2).

book_ref.quote: In this way, the new DNA is surrounded by two membranes

blocks.prompt: 27 During sporulation, a new peptidoglycan layer forms:
blocks.explanation: A new peptidoglycan layer forms between the membranes around the separated DNA and cytoplasm; a spore coat then forms around it (2.2).

book_ref.quote: A new peptidoglycan layer forms between the membranes around separated DNA and cytoplasm

blocks.prompt: 28 During sporulation, what happens to the DNA of the vegetative cell?
blocks.explanation: The DNA of the vegetative cell disintegrates and the whole cell begins to dehydrate (2.2).

book_ref.quote: The DNA of vegetative cell disintegrates and whole cell begins to dehydrate

blocks.prompt: 29 Under favourable conditions, an endospore:

options.text: germinates into a new vegetative cell

blocks.explanation: Endospores remain dormant until favourable conditions return, then germinate into a new vegetative cell (2.2).

book_ref.quote: Under favourable conditions, endospore germinates to give rise to a new vegetative cell

blocks.prompt: 30 Most bacilli and spirilla bacteria move by means of:
blocks.explanation: Most bacilli and spirilla move by flagella; they swim using them (2.3).

book_ref.quote: Most bacilli and spirilla bacteria move by means of flagella

blocks.prompt: 31 When a whole bacterial population moves together by means of flagella, the movement is called:
blocks.explanation: Movement of a bacterial population together by flagella is swarming (2.3).

book_ref.quote: When a bacterial population moves together by means of flagella, the movement is called swarming

blocks.prompt: 32 The cell is pushed forward with the flagellum trailing behind when the flagellum rotates:
blocks.explanation: Counter clockwise rotation of the flagellum pushes the cell forward with the flagellum trailing behind (2.3).

book_ref.quote: Counter clockwise rotation of flagellum pushes the cell forward

blocks.prompt: 33 In gliding movement, bacteria move smoothly over solid surfaces by:
blocks.explanation: In gliding, bacteria secrete a slimy substance that helps smooth gliding over solid surfaces (2.3).

book_ref.quote: In gliding, bacteria secrete slimy substance

blocks.prompt: 34 Sliding movement in bacteria is due to:

options.text: the pushing force of dividing cells

blocks.explanation: Sliding is due to the expansion created by the pushing force of dividing cells (2.3).

book_ref.quote: It is due to the expansion created by the pushing force of dividing cells

blocks.prompt: 35 Streptococcus, which has no flagella or pili, moves by:
blocks.explanation: Some bacteria like Streptococcus without flagella or pili move by Brownian movement, due to random movement of fluid particles (2.3).

book_ref.quote: Some bacteria (e.g., Streptococcus) that do not have flagella or pili

blocks.prompt: 36 The axial filament of spirochaetes runs length-wise in the:
blocks.explanation: The axial filament, a modified flagellum, runs length-wise in the periplasmic space between cell membrane and outer membrane (2.3).

book_ref.quote: It is anchored at one end and runs length-wise in periplasmic space

blocks.prompt: 37 Bacteria that do not possess flagella are called:
blocks.explanation: Bacteria without flagella are atrichous (2.5).

book_ref.quote: The bacteria which do not possess flagella are called atrichous

blocks.prompt: 38 A bacterium with a single polar flagellum is:
blocks.explanation: Bacteria with a single polar flagellum are monotrichous (2.5).

book_ref.quote: The bacteria with single polar flagellum are called monotrichous

blocks.prompt: 39 Bacteria with a tuft of flagella at one pole are called:
blocks.explanation: A tuft of flagella at one pole is lophotrichous; flagella at both poles is amphitrichous (2.5).

book_ref.quote: The bacteria with a tuft of flagella at one pole are called lophotrichous

blocks.prompt: 40 Amphitrichous bacteria have:

options.text: flagella at each of the two poles

blocks.explanation: Amphitrichous bacteria have flagella at each of the two poles (2.5).

book_ref.quote: The bacteria with flagella at each of two poles are called amphitrichous

blocks.prompt: 41 Bacteria with flagella surrounding the whole cell are:
blocks.explanation: Flagella surrounding the whole cell: peritrichous (2.5).

book_ref.quote: The bacteria with flagella surrounding the whole cell are called peritrichous

blocks.prompt: 42 Bacterial flagella are composed of:
blocks.explanation: Bacterial flagella are not built on the 9+2 microtubule pattern of eukaryotes; they are made of flagellin protein (2.5).

book_ref.quote: They are not built on 9+2 pattern of microtubules, but are composed of flagellin protein

blocks.prompt: 43 The three parts of a bacterial flagellum are:
blocks.explanation: The bacterial flagellum consists of a basal body, a hook and a filament (2.5).

book_ref.quote: The bacterial flagellum consists of a basal body, a hook and a filament

blocks.prompt: 44 The basal body of the flagellum of a Gram-negative bacterium has:
blocks.explanation: The basal body has rotating rings: one pair in Gram-positive and two pairs in Gram-negative bacteria (2.5).

book_ref.quote: one pair in Gram-positive bacteria and two pairs in Gram-negative bacteria

blocks.prompt: 45 The part of a bacterial flagellum that connects the basal body with the filament is the:
blocks.explanation: The hook is a curved structure connecting the basal body with the filament (2.5).

book_ref.quote: The hook is a curved structure that connects basal body with the filament

blocks.prompt: 46 Pili are involved in attachment to surfaces and in:
blocks.explanation: Pili are used for attachment and are involved in conjugation (mating) between cells (2.5).

book_ref.quote: They are also involved in the mating process (conjugation) between cells

blocks.prompt: 47 The fossil record shows that prokaryotes were abundant:
blocks.explanation: Fossils show prokaryotes (archaea and bacteria) were abundant 3.5 billion years ago (2.6).

book_ref.quote: were abundant 3.5 billion years ago

blocks.prompt: 48 After appearing, prokaryotes remained all alone on Earth for the next:
blocks.explanation: Prokaryotes evolved and remained alone on Earth for the next 2 billion years (2.6).

book_ref.quote: They evolved and remained all alone on Earth for the next 2 billion years

blocks.prompt: 49 Margulis and Schwartz classified all prokaryotes into:
blocks.explanation: Margulis and Schwartz classified all prokaryotes into 16 phyla (2.6).

book_ref.quote: They classified them into 16 phyla

blocks.prompt: 50 Rigid, rod-shaped, heterotrophic, Gram-negative bacteria that include Escherichia coli and vibrios are:
blocks.explanation: Omnibacteria are rigid, rod-shaped, heterotrophic, Gram-negative; E. coli is an example and vibrios are included (2.6).

book_ref.quote: These are rigid, rod-shaped, heterotrophic, Gram-negative bacteria

blocks.prompt: 51 Which statement about omnibacteria is correct?

options.text: they do not produce spores and are usually aerobic

blocks.explanation: Omnibacteria mostly have flagella, do not produce spores and are usually aerobic (2.6).

book_ref.quote: They do not produce spores

blocks.prompt: 52 Cyanobacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen in special cells called:
blocks.explanation: Many cyanobacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen in special cells called heterocysts (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Many cyanobacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen in their special cells called heterocysts

blocks.prompt: 53 Besides chlorophyll-a, cyanobacteria contain accessory pigments such as:

options.text: carotenoids and blue and red phycobilins

blocks.explanation: Cyanobacteria contain chlorophyll-a and accessory pigments like carotenoids and blue and red phycobilins (2.6).

book_ref.quote: They contain chlorophyll-a and accessory pigments like carotenoids, and blue and red phycobilins

blocks.prompt: 54 In the history of the Earth, cyanobacteria played the most important role in:

options.text: increasing free oxygen in the atmosphere

blocks.explanation: Cyanobacteria played the most important role in increasing free oxygen in the atmosphere (2.6).

book_ref.quote: They played most important role in the history of the Earth for increasing free oxygen in atmosphere

blocks.prompt: 55 According to a recent discovery, the bulk of modern petroleum deposits were formed by masses of decayed:
blocks.explanation: The bulk of modern petroleum deposits were formed by masses of decayed cyanobacteria (2.6).

book_ref.quote: the bulk of our modern petroleum deposits were formed by masses of decayed cyanobacteria

blocks.prompt: 56 The colours of blooms in polluted water result from:
blocks.explanation: Colourful blooms come from rampant growth of cyanobacteria; their colours result from its photosynthetic pigments (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Colourful blooms may occur in polluted water as a result of the rampant growth of cyanobacteria

blocks.prompt: 57 Mycoplasmas are resistant to penicillin because they:
blocks.explanation: Lacking cell walls, mycoplasmas and spiroplasmas resist penicillin and antibiotics that inhibit cell wall growth (2.6).

book_ref.quote: they are resistant to penicillin and other antibiotics that work by inhibiting cell wall growth

blocks.prompt: 58 The lethal yellowing disease of coconuts is caused by:
blocks.explanation: Spiroplasmas cause significant plant diseases such as lethal yellowing of coconuts (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Spiroplasmas cause significant plant diseases e.g., the lethal yellowing disease of coconuts

blocks.prompt: 59 Spirochaetes are long spirilla with Gram-negative walls and may have:
blocks.explanation: Spirochaetes may have 2 to more than 100 flagella; Treponema is an important example (2.6).

book_ref.quote: They may have 2 to more than 100 flagella

blocks.prompt: 60 Syphilis is caused by:
blocks.explanation: Treponema, an important spirochaete, causes syphilis (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Treponema are important spirochaetes

blocks.prompt: 61 Pseudomonas aeruginosa is usually harmless but can form serious infections in:
blocks.explanation: Pseudomonas aeruginosa occurs in soil, water and raw vegetables; usually harmless, it can cause serious infections in weak people (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Pseudomonas aeruginosa occurs in soil, water and raw vegetables

blocks.prompt: 62 Straight or curved Gram-negative rods with one or many flagella at one end, some of which take part in denitrification, are:
blocks.explanation: Pseudomonads are straight or curved Gram-negative rods with flagella at one end; some play a role in denitrification (2.6).

book_ref.quote: These are straight or curved Gram-negative rods with one or many flagella at one end

blocks.prompt: 63 Bacteria with filamentous growth forms and resistant spores are:
blocks.explanation: Actinomycetes have filamentous growth forms and produce spores resistant to unfavourable conditions (2.6).

book_ref.quote: These have filamentous growth forms

blocks.prompt: 64 Leprosy is caused by:
blocks.explanation: Mycobacterium leprae, an actinomycete, causes leprosy; Mycobacterium tuberculosis causes tuberculosis (2.6).

book_ref.quote: A member of this group i.e., Mycobacterium leprae causes leprosy

blocks.prompt: 65 Some actinomycetes are responsible for:

options.text: dental plaque, in which tooth enamel is destroyed

blocks.explanation: Some actinomycetes cause dental plaque, in which the enamel of teeth is destroyed (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Some actinomycetes are responsible for dental plaque

blocks.prompt: 66 About how many new antibiotics from actinomycetes are discovered each year?
blocks.explanation: About 150 new antibiotics from actinomycetes are being discovered each year (2.6).

book_ref.quote: About 150 new antibiotics from actinomycetes are being discovered each year

blocks.prompt: 67 Nitrogen-fixing actinomycetes are found in:

options.text: the root nodules of many flowering plants

blocks.explanation: Some actinomycetes are nitrogen fixers and are found in the root nodules of many flowering plants (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Some actinomycetes are nitrogen fixers and are found in the root nodules of many flowering plants

blocks.prompt: 68 Azotobacter, found in soil and water, belongs to which group?
blocks.explanation: Azotobacter is a nitrogen-fixing aerobic bacterium; it fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia (book correction) (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Azotobacter is a member of this group

blocks.prompt: 69 Azotobacter fixes atmospheric nitrogen into:
blocks.explanation: Azotobacter fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia; nitrifying bacteria then turn ammonia into nitrite and nitrate (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Azotobacter fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia

blocks.prompt: 70 Chemosynthetic bacteria derive energy from:

options.text: oxidation of inorganic compounds of nitrogen, sulphur and iron

blocks.explanation: Chemosynthetic bacteria oxidize inorganic nitrogen, sulphur and iron compounds and use the energy to make food (2.6).

book_ref.quote: These bacteria derive energy from the oxidation of inorganic compounds of nitrogen, sulphur and iron

blocks.prompt: 71 Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are:
blocks.explanation: Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are chemosynthetic; they oxidize NH₃ and it is converted to nitrite and nitrate (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are included in this group

blocks.prompt: 72 In the table of bacterial groups, cyanobacteria are shown with which nutrition and ecological role?
blocks.explanation: The table lists cyanobacteria as P (photosynthetic), carbon and nitrogen fixers (2.6).

book_ref.quote: Carbon and nitrogen fixers

blocks.prompt: 73 The effects of bacteria on life on Earth are:
blocks.explanation: Bacteria have beneficial as well as harmful effects on life on Earth (2.7).

book_ref.quote: They have beneficial as well as harmful effects on life on Earth

blocks.prompt: 74 Which bacterium is named as a denitrifying bacterium?
blocks.explanation: Pseudomonas is a denitrifying bacterium; Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are nitrifying (2.7).

book_ref.quote: denitrifying bacteria (Pseudomonas)

blocks.prompt: 75 Decomposer bacteria play a key role in the:
blocks.explanation: Decomposer bacteria decompose dead organic matter and play a key role in the carbon-hydrogen-oxygen cycle (2.7).

book_ref.quote: Decomposer bacteria decompose dead organic matter and play key role in carbon-hydrogen-oxygen cycle

blocks.prompt: 76 Which bacterium, with yeasts and molds, has been used for thousands of years to make fermented foods like yogurt and cheese?
blocks.explanation: Lactobacillus with yeasts and molds is used for fermented foods such as cheese, pickles, soy sauce, vinegar, wine and yogurt (2.7).

book_ref.quote: Lactobacillus in combination with yeasts and molds

blocks.prompt: 77 Bacteria are used commercially in the preparation of:
blocks.explanation: Commercial preparation of animal skins for leather goods involves bacteria (2.7).

book_ref.quote: Commercial preparation of animals’ skin for making leather goods, involves the use of bacteria

blocks.prompt: 78 The use of bacteria to remove or degrade pollutants from the environment is called:
blocks.explanation: Removal or degradation of pollutants by bacteria is bioremediation, e.g., sewage, oil spills, toxic wastes (2.7).

book_ref.quote: Such bacteria have been used for the removal or degradation of pollutants (bioremediation)

blocks.prompt: 79 Bacteria that digest hydrocarbons present in petroleum are used to:
blocks.explanation: Bacteria that digest petroleum hydrocarbons are used to clean up oil spills (2.7).

book_ref.quote: Some bacteria can digest the hydrocarbons present in petroleum

blocks.prompt: 80 The bacterium commonly used as a biopesticide is:
blocks.explanation: Biological pest control commonly uses Bacillus thuringiensis, a Gram-positive soil bacterium (2.7).

book_ref.quote: This commonly involves Bacillus thuringiensis

blocks.prompt: 81 Bacterial biopesticides are preferred because they:

options.text: are environmentally friendly with little or no effect on humans and pollinators
remain in soil permanently as poisons

blocks.explanation: Biopesticides are environmentally friendly and have little or no effect on humans, wildlife, pollinators and most beneficial insects (2.7).

book_ref.quote: These biopesticides are environmentally friendly

blocks.prompt: 82 By inserting human genes in bacteria, scientists produce therapeutic proteins such as:
blocks.explanation: Human genes inserted in bacteria produce therapeutic proteins such as insulin, growth hormones or antibodies (2.7).

book_ref.quote: Scientists also insert human genes in bacteria and produce therapeutic proteins

blocks.prompt: 83 The mixture of organisms regularly found at any anatomical site is called:
blocks.explanation: The mixture of organisms regularly found at an anatomical site is the normal flora (2.8).

book_ref.quote: The mixture of organisms regularly found at any anatomical site is referred to as the normal flora

blocks.prompt: 84 In a healthy animal, which tissues are normally free of microorganisms?
blocks.explanation: Internal tissues such as blood, brain and muscle are normally free of microorganisms; surface tissues are colonized (2.8).

book_ref.quote: In a healthy animal, the internal tissues, e.g., blood, brain, muscle, etc., are normally free of microorganisms

blocks.prompt: 85 The most numerous and obvious microbial components of the human normal flora are:
blocks.explanation: Normal flora includes bacteria, a few fungi and protists, and some methanogenic archaea; bacteria are the most numerous (2.8).

book_ref.quote: Bacteria are the most numerous and obvious microbial components of normal flora

blocks.prompt: 86 The association between humans and their normal flora is:
blocks.explanation: The association is mutualistic: the flora get nutrients, a stable environment, constant temperature, protection and transport, and the body benefits too (2.8).

book_ref.quote: The associations between humans and their normal flora are mutualistic

blocks.prompt: 87 Enteric bacteria of the human gut secrete:
blocks.explanation: Enteric bacteria secrete vitamin K and vitamin B₁₂; lactic acid bacteria produce certain B-vitamins (2.8).

book_ref.quote: enteric bacteria secrete Vitamin K and Vitamin B₁₂

blocks.prompt: 88 Normal flora prevents colonization by pathogens mainly by:

options.text: competing with them for attachment sites and nutrients

blocks.explanation: Normal flora compete with pathogens for attachment sites and nutrients, so pathogens have less chance of entering tissues (2.8).

book_ref.quote: The bacteria of normal flora compete with pathogens for attachment sites and nutrients

blocks.prompt: 89 Antibodies produced at low levels against the normal flora protect the body because they:
blocks.explanation: Normal flora act as antigens; low levels of antibodies against them cross-react with certain pathogens and prevent infection (2.8).

book_ref.quote: Low levels of antibodies produced against the normal flora are known to cross-react with certain pathogens

blocks.prompt: 90 Viruses represent creatures that:

options.text: lack cellular organization yet show some characteristics of living things

blocks.explanation: Viruses do not possess cellular organization yet show some characteristics of living things (2.9).

book_ref.quote: there are some creatures that do not possess cellular organization yet show some characteristics of livings

blocks.prompt: 91 Viruses range in size from:
blocks.explanation: Viruses range from 20 nm (parvovirus) to 250 nm (pox viruses) (2.9).

book_ref.quote: They range in size from 20 nm (parvovirus) to 250 nm (pox viruses)

blocks.prompt: 92 Viruses are smaller than most bacteria by about:
blocks.explanation: Viruses are 10 to 1000 times smaller than most bacteria and can only be seen under an electron microscope (2.9).

book_ref.quote: They are 10 to 1000 times smaller than most bacteria

blocks.prompt: 93 The protein subunits that make up the capsid are called:
blocks.explanation: The capsid is made of protein subunits called capsomeres; their number and kind are characteristic of a virus (2.9).

book_ref.quote: Capsid is made up of protein subunits called as capsomeres

blocks.prompt: 94 The central core and capsid of a virus together are called:
blocks.explanation: Central core and capsid are collectively called the nucleocapsid (2.9).

book_ref.quote: Central core and capsid are collectively called as nucleocapsid

blocks.prompt: 95 The capsid of adenovirus contains:
blocks.explanation: Adenovirus (common cold) has 252 capsomeres; herpes virus has 162 (2.9).

book_ref.quote: Adenovirus (causes common cold) contains 252 capsomeres in its capsid

blocks.prompt: 96 Herpes virus, which causes cold sores and chickenpox, has how many capsomeres in its capsid?
blocks.explanation: Herpes virus contains 162 capsomeres in its capsid (2.9).

book_ref.quote: Herpes virus (causes cold sores, chickenpox etc.) contains 162 capsomeres in its capsid

blocks.prompt: 97 The envelope of some animal viruses is a lipid-rich membrane derived from:
blocks.explanation: The envelope is a lipid-rich membrane derived from the host cell (2.9).

book_ref.quote: It is a lipid-rich membrane and is derived from host cell

blocks.prompt: 98 Viruses without an envelope are known as:
blocks.explanation: Non-enveloped viruses are known as naked viruses (2.9).

book_ref.quote: Non enveloped viruses are known as naked-viruses

blocks.prompt: 99 An icosahedral virus has:
blocks.explanation: Bacteriophages may be cubical, icosahedral (20 faces), helical or complex (2.9).

book_ref.quote: The bacterial viruses (bacteriophages) may be cubical, icosahedral (having 20 faces), helical, or complex

blocks.prompt: 100 The best known phages of Escherichia coli are:
blocks.explanation: The best known phages of E. coli are T-phages; there are many varieties (2.9).

book_ref.quote: The best known phages of Escherichia coli are T-phages

blocks.prompt: 101 The core of the T4 phage head contains:
blocks.explanation: The T4 head's capsid is protein, while the core contains a long double stranded DNA (2.9).

book_ref.quote: Its capsid is made of proteins while core contains a long double stranded DNA

blocks.prompt: 102 How many tail fibres are attached with the end plate of a T4 phage?
blocks.explanation: Six tail fibres attached to the end plate help the phage attach to the bacterial wall (2.9).

book_ref.quote: Six tail fibres are attached with end plate

blocks.prompt: 103 In the T4 phage, the sheath is attached to the head by the:
blocks.explanation: A neck attaches the sheath with the head; an end plate is on the other side of the sheath (2.9).

book_ref.quote: A neck attaches sheath with head

blocks.prompt: 104 Transgenic bacteria are those whose genome has:
blocks.explanation: Transgenic bacteria have DNA of some other organism in their genome, e.g., a gene carried in by a bacteriophage (2.9).

book_ref.quote: Such transgenic bacteria (transgenic: whose genome has DNA of some other organism)

blocks.prompt: 105 HIV belongs to the group of:
blocks.explanation: HIV belongs to the retroviruses, a special group of animal viruses (2.9).

book_ref.quote: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) belongs to the group called retroviruses

blocks.prompt: 106 HIV particles are spherical and about:
blocks.explanation: Retroviruses like HIV are spherical and about 100 nm in diameter (2.9).

book_ref.quote: They are spherical in form and are about 100 nm in diameter

blocks.prompt: 107 The glycoprotein spikes on the HIV envelope help the virus to:

options.text: identify and bind to its target
